title: Mattel Brick Shop’s Hot Wheels Racer Series Kits Are Like DIY Hot Wheels Cars

body_markdown:
If you’ve ever picked up a Hot Wheels car and thought, “I wish I could build it myself,” Mattel Brick Shop has what you’re looking for. The brand announced a range of 1/64-scale kits called Hot Wheels Racer Series that are small, affordable, and easy to build.


The cars in the Hot Wheels Racer Series are the smallest and most affordable kits offered by Mattel Brick Shop, which was created in 2025 to take on LEGO. The initial range includes a 2024 Chevrolet Camaro ZL1, a 2018 Audi TT RS, a Maserati MCPura, a 1991 Acura NSX, a 1999 Honda S2000, and a hot rod called Hot Wheels Bone Shaker. Each kit consists of fewer than 30 parts, so they’re relatively simple to build. For context,[Mattel Brick Shop’s 1/12-scale Lamborghini Miura](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/mattel-brick-shop-lamborghini-miura-pricing-pictures-availability/) is made up of 1524 pieces.

While the Hot Wheels-sized kits aren’t as detailed as Mattel Brick Shop’s bigger and more expensive cars, they’re accurate enough to look like the car they’re modeled after. They feature metal base plates, rolling wheels, and kit-specific pieces that replicate key styling cues. The curved shape of the TT’s silhouette is spot on, for example, while the NSX’s rear spoiler is surprisingly realistic.


The new Hot Wheels Racer Series kits will go on sale nationwide in January 2027, and they’re priced at $4.99 each. The range will grow quickly: Mattel Brick Shop expects to offer 20 cars by the end of 2027. Finding the one that you’re after may be easier said than done, however. The kits will be distributed randomly in individual boxes, so you won’t know what’s in it until you open it.
